correctness.rationale: For r=e^{-2t} in (0,1), direct product of the exact symmetric three-edge heat matrices has stationary eigenvalue 1, determinant r^3, other-eigenvalue trace tau=-(1+r)(r^2-10r+1)/8 and discriminant (1-r)^4(r^2-14r+1)/64. The unique discriminant root in (0,1) is r*=7-4sqrt(3). For r>r*, conjugate eigenvalues have radius r^(3/2), strictly increasing with r. For 0<r<r*, the negative-real-root maximum is a sum of two positive terms strictly decreasing with r. Thus the unique per-complete-sweep minimizer is t*=log(2+sqrt(3)), radius 26-15sqrt(3)=(2-sqrt(3))^3; limiting full-equilibration rate is 1/8. Nonzero skew entry T_12-T_21=-(1-r)^2(1+r)/8 excludes a scalar diagonalizable double eigenvalue and proves the exceptional-point Jordan defect. This is spectral asymptotic per sweep, not total elapsed diffusion time or fixed-k transient norm.

value.rationale: This is an exact global one-parameter optimization for the smallest cycle with three strictly positive-definite reversible local heat factors. The finite optimal damping and nontrivial defective boundary distinguish per-sweep asymptotics from the intuitive full-equilibration limit and expose a motivated effect for systematic Markov scans and cyclic splitting.
